header.activation_event: booking_received (the user's candidate, not yet tested against week-4 retention)
header.grade_math: 100 - 5 (Measurement, warn) - 12 (Onboarding completion, fail) - 5 (Activation and time to value, warn) - 5 (Segments, warn) - 5 (Onboarding emails, warn) = 68

headline: Setup is the biggest drop: 43.0% of the 1,536 new signups finish the wizard and publish a booking page, and the calendar step loses the most of them (1,250 added services, 690 connected a calendar) (call 5).
On mobile, 21.9% of signups finish setup against 50.0% on desktop, and mobile brings 44.9% of new users (call 6).
28.0% of signups get a first client booking, and 6.0% of booking user-days fall on day 0 (calls 5 and 7). booking_received fires but isn't a key event yet (call 1).

journey_map.note: At least, because pricing (3,420) and demo (610) users can't be added together. No step rate: a visitor can reach pricing without an engaged visit, so the two don't nest.
No step rate for the same reason: the signup page can be reached straight from an ad or a link.
Share of the signup page's new users; signup happens on that page, so the two nest.
Week-1 return is in the Early return area.

fix_first: Stage 6, Onboard: 43.0% of signups finish setup, the lowest step rate on the map. Inside the wizard, the step from services_added (1,250) to calendar_connected (690) loses 560 users, the most of any step.

weekly_new_users.source: call 5: first_visit users summed by first-session week
weekly_new_users.flagged_weeks: none: no week is 3 or more times the median of the others
weekly_new_users.rows_left_out: 14 (not set) first-session rows and 3,880 rows of users who first came before 2026-08-03

scorecard.key_number: booking_received fires, not a key event
scorecard.why: The property sees both the site and the app (2 hosts, no test host), signup and all four setup steps fire, and weekly new users are steady. The activation event fired for 430 new users but isn't one of the 2 key events.

scorecard.key_number: 13.7% of new users reach the signup page
scorecard.why: 2,950 of 21,600 new users opened the signup page, above your own floor of 12% (SKILL.md sets no threshold for this area, so your target is used).
660 of 1,536 signups published a booking page, under the 50% fail line.
430 of 1,536 signups got a client booking, in the 20% to 40% warn band; only 6.0% of booking user-days are on day 0, so the first session rarely ends with value.
2,274 of 19,762 new users in cohorts w01-w11 came back in week 1, above your floor of 10%; 6.1% came back in week 4 (cohorts w01-w08).
Mobile brings 44.9% of new users and finishes setup at under half the desktop rate; the gap (28.1 points) is far above the 5.6-point threshold.
'Welcome series' goes to every new account on day 0, 2 and 5 whatever they did; nothing is triggered by a step done or skipped.

top_fixes.fix: Let people publish the booking page before connecting a calendar
top_fixes.loss_counted_as: signups who never finished setup (876), x 30 / 84 days
top_fixes.pattern: inside the setup steps: a short guided setup that shows progress, saves partial work, lets people skip a step and come back, and asks only for what the first result needs
top_fixes.what: Make calendar sync a skippable step that the app asks for again after the first booking, and show progress ('Step 3 of 4') with saved answers. Services and opening hours are all a booking page needs to go live.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 5: services_added 1,250, calendar_connected 690, tutorial_complete 660. Call 8: the calendar connection guide is the most-read help page (412 new users) and calendar troubleshooting comes next (236).
top_fixes.expected_impact: stage 6, going after about 313 signups a month who stop before the booking page is live
top_fixes.effort: medium: a product change to the wizard

top_fixes.fix: Trigger the setup emails on what people did, not on the day
top_fixes.loss_counted_as: the same stage as fix 1: signups who never finished setup
top_fixes.pattern: emails after signup triggered by what the user did or didn't do
top_fixes.what: Replace the fixed day-2 and day-5 emails with: setup started but not finished after a day (a link back to the step they left, with the calendar guide), booking page live (share it now), and no booking after about a week (ask what's in the way). Send sign_up, tutorial_complete and booking_received to Klaviyo so the triggers work.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 12: the day-2 'Connect your calendar' email reached 1,420 people in 90 days at a 9% click rate. It goes out on a fixed day, so it also reaches people who connected a calendar on day 0.
top_fixes.expected_impact: stage 6, the same users as fix 1, reached by email when they leave the app
top_fixes.effort: medium: a flow in Klaviyo plus the events sent to it

top_fixes.fix: Make the setup wizard work on a phone
top_fixes.loss_counted_as: mobile signups who never finished setup (328), x 30 / 84 days
top_fixes.pattern: if mobile users stall, the first run must work on a phone
top_fixes.what: Test each wizard step on a phone, starting with the calendar connection (it opens a sign-in window that is easy to lose on mobile), and let people finish setup on desktop with a 'send me a link' option.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 6: mobile 92 of 420 signups finished setup (21.9%), desktop 575 of 1,150 (50.0%).
top_fixes.expected_impact: stage 6 on mobile, about 117 signups a month

top_fixes.fix: Turn the empty dashboard into a 'get your first booking' checklist
top_fixes.loss_counted_as: users who published a booking page but got no booking (230), x 30 / 84 days
top_fixes.pattern: after setup, before first value: one clear first action; slow time to value: a short checklist with visible progress
top_fixes.what: After the page goes live, show 4 small tasks: copy the booking link, add it to the Instagram bio, add it to the Google Business profile, send it to 5 regular clients. Mark each as done.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 5: 660 finished setup, 430 got a booking. Call 7: 6.0% of booking user-days on day 0, 24.8% on days 3 to 7.
top_fixes.expected_impact: stage 7, about 82 users a month who are set up but have no client booking yet

top_fixes.fix: Mark booking_received as a key event
top_fixes.users_lost_per_month: can't be counted: it changes what GA4 reports, not what users do
top_fixes.what: So activation shows up in GA4's standard reports and can be imported to the ad platforms as a conversion.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 1: key events are sign_up, purchase; call 3: booking_received fired in the window.
top_fixes.expected_impact: activation counted next to signups in every GA4 report
top_fixes.who: I can do this now, with your yes

help_pages_read_by_new_users.dropped_pages: 1 blog post that only mentions pricing in its path (/blog/salon-pricing-guide/), and 1 help path that GA4 returned cut short, so its page can't be told
help_pages_read_by_new_users.reading: The most-read help pages are about connecting and syncing a calendar, the step where the wizard loses the most people. Pages can't be added together, so each type shows its most-read page.

time_to_value.counts: user-days, not people: a user who does an event on 3 days counts 3 times, and booking_received repeats with every booking

feature_adoption.note: GA4 doesn't know the order, so this is how many activated users also bought a plan, not when.

activation_repeat_use.reading: Businesses that get one booking keep getting them, so the activation event turns into a habit once it happens.

measurement_plan: Not needed: every stage is tracked. The one change is marking booking_received as a key event (fix 5).

messages.message: Welcome: set up your booking page

onboarding_emails.conversions: not read: Klaviyo counts conversions against Placed Order, and the product doesn't send the activation event to Klaviyo yet
plan: right after signup: welcome and one link that opens the setup wizard where they left it
setup started, not finished after a day: a link back to the step they left, with the calendar guide if that is the step
booking page live: share it now, with the link ready to copy
page live, no booking after about a week: ask what's in the way, and offer a short call
first booking received: well done, here's how to cut no-shows with reminders
onboarding_emails.gaps: Every current message goes out on a fixed day. Nothing reacts to setup done, setup skipped or a first booking.

personalisation_opportunities.tailored_experience: a phone-first wizard, or a 'finish on your computer' email with a link straight back to the step they left
open on the promise of the ad they clicked (most search ads sell online booking): the booking page preview first, with setup steps after it

personalisation_opportunities.number: 412 new users on the calendar connection guide
personalisation_opportunities.tailored_experience: offer 'skip for now' at the calendar step and a one-click connection test, with the guide beside it
none: its setup rate is 3.6 points below the rest, inside the 11.0-point threshold, so the gap isn't real

onboarding_model: Self-serve: low monthly prices and many signups, so the wizard, the first screens and the emails carry the load. A short setup call for the Business plan is worth a test later.

offered.why: booking_received fires and isn't a key event
none of the 3 existing audiences covers it; 1,106 new signups in the window had no booking
